## `DeferredActionQueue`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.DeferredActionQueue` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The actions scenes deferred (`cwy.defer`), released only when the room is quiet: no scene is playing (so the asking scene has ended), the room's main state is `Idle` (so a long story's fade and tidy are done), and both have held for [`DeferredActionQueue.SettleSeconds`](#deferredactionqueue--settleseconds) (so the game's own end-of-talk handling, one frame later, has run first). Pure: the game side says whether the room is quiet; time is passed in. Thread-safe.

## `ScenarioBuiltInArgs`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioBuiltInArgs` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the four framework commands read from their row, shared by the runtime's handlers and by [`ScenarioLint`](#scenariolint) so a row the lint passes is a row the handler accepts. Every built-in reads its words from `Arg1`:

- **`cwy.do` (5000)**: `<action> [name=value ...]` ([`ScriptActionLine`](#scriptactionline)); runs it now and holds the scene until it answers.
- **`cwy.defer` (5001)**: the same line; runs it after the scene ends and the room is idle.
- **`cwy.wait` (5002)**: seconds, invariant (`1.5`), more than 0 and at most 300.
- **`cwy.flag` (5003)**: `set <name>` or `clear <name>` ([`ScenarioFlags`](#scenarioflags)).

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioCommandContext` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

<a id="scenariocommandhandler"></a>

## `ScenarioCommandHandler`

delegate · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioCommandHandler` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

```csharp
delegate virtual void ScenarioCommandHandler(IScenarioCommandContext context)
```

Runs one script-command row. Called on the Unity main thread by the script-command runtime when the game's reader reaches a row whose command is this one.

The contract, which the runtime enforces:

- Decide at most once: [`IScenarioCommandContext.Continue`](#iscenariocommandcontext--continue), [`IScenarioCommandContext.JumpTo`](#iscenariocommandcontext--jumpto) or [`IScenarioCommandContext.WaitFor`](#iscenariocommandcontext--waitfor). Later calls are ignored with a warning.
- Returning without deciding means [`IScenarioCommandContext.Continue`](#iscenariocommandcontext--continue).
- Throwing is logged against the owner and the scene continues with the next row: a broken command never stalls a scene.
- Keep it short. Long work belongs in [`IScenarioCommandContext.WaitFor`](#iscenariocommandcontext--waitfor) or in a deferred action.

**Parameters**

- `context`: The row and the three ways to go on.

<a id="scenariocommandids"></a>

## `ScenarioCommandIds`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioCommandIds` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The number range of script commands CWY:LS Mod Loader adds to the game's `CommandType` (50 members, 0-1000) and the fixed numbers of the framework's own commands.

5000-5999 lies outside every game value. The game's `ScenarioReader.ReadSentence` switch falls through an unknown value and stalls, so these rows are only safe once the script-command prefix is installed ([`ScenarioCommandRegistry.RuntimeAvailable`](#scenariocommandregistry--runtimeavailable)); its pre-scan ignores unknown commands.

5000-5099 is the framework's: fixed numbers, so `"Command": 5000` in a pack means `cwy.do` in every session. 5100-5999 is handed out by name, in order of first use, to mods' commands and to names nobody has registered yet; those numbers are per session, so packs name them (`"Command": "my.mod.wave"`), never number them.

<a id="scenariocommandids--camerapreset"></a>

### `const int CameraPreset = 5010`

`cwy.camera.preset` (camera control).

<a id="scenariocommandids--camerapresetname"></a>

### `const string CameraPresetName = "cwy.camera.preset"`

Name of [`ScenarioCommandIds.CameraPreset`](#scenariocommandids--camerapreset).

<a id="scenariocommandids--camerareset"></a>

### `const int CameraReset = 5012`

`cwy.camera.reset` (camera control).

<a id="scenariocommandregistry"></a>

## `ScenarioCommandRegistry`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioCommandRegistry` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Script commands by name and number: pack rows name a command (`"Command": "cwy.do"`), the pack parser turns the name into a number in 5000-5999 ([`ScenarioCommandRegistry.TryResolve`](#scenariocommandregistry--tryresolve-string-ref-int)), and the script-command runtime looks the number up when the game's reader reaches the row. An ordinary object so it can be tested; [`ScenarioCommandRegistry.Shared`](#scenariocommandregistry--shared) is the one the game uses. Thread-safe.

**Numbers.** The framework's commands have fixed numbers ([`ScenarioCommandIds.BuiltIns`](#scenariocommandids--builtins), 5000-5099). Any other valid name gets the next free number from 5100 on the first time it is resolved or registered, and keeps it for the session even if its handler goes away, so rows parsed before a mod loaded still point at the right command. A number outside 5000-5999 is never handed out.

**Owners.** The framework ([`ScenarioCommandRegistry.FrameworkOwner`](#scenariocommandregistry--frameworkowner)) registers `cwy.*` names; a mod registers only names that start with `<its id>.` and never a built-in name. A number has at most one handler: a second registration is refused until the first is disposed.

<a id="scenariocommandrunner"></a>

## `ScenarioCommandRunner`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioCommandRunner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Runs one script-command row: finds the handler, calls it with a [`ScenarioCommandContext`](#scenariocommandcontext), and turns whatever happened into a [`ScenarioCommandDecision`](#scenariocommanddecision). A row with no handler and a handler that throws both continue with the next row (with a warning): a broken command never stalls a scene. Pure; the game side applies the decision.

<a id="scenariocommandrunner--run"></a>

### `static ScenarioCommandDecision Run(ScenarioCommandRegistry registry, ScenarioCommandRow row, string scenarioType, Func<string, bool> hasRow, Action<string> warn)`

Runs one row.

**Parameters**

- `registry`: Where the handler is looked up.
- `row`: The row.
- `scenarioType`: The group's scene type name.
- `hasRow`: True when the group has a row with this id; null accepts every id.
- `warn`: Where warnings go (no handler, a throw, contract breaches); null drops them.

**Returns:** The decision; never null.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `registry` or `row` is null.

<a id="scenarioflags"></a>

## `ScenarioFlags`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioFlags` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The named flags scripts and mods set (`cwy.flag set|clear <name>`, the Scenes facet) and the `flag:<name>` condition reads. A flag is either set or not. Names follow the condition argument rule (1-64 letters, digits, `_ . -`; checked by [`ConditionParser.TryParseKey`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Conditions.md#conditionparser--tryparsekey)) and compare case-insensitively. An ordinary object so it can be tested; [`ScenarioFlags.Shared`](#scenarioflags--shared) is the one the game uses. Thread-safe.

Flags live in CWY:LS Mod Loader's own data file (the game side saves [`ScenarioFlags.ToJson`](#scenarioflags--tojson) to `BepInEx/data/script/flags.json`), never in the game's save, so a vanilla game and Steam Cloud never see them.

<a id="scenariolint"></a>

## `ScenarioLint`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioLint` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Checks pack scenes for the pitfalls the game's reader has and for script-command rows that would not run. Advisory: nothing is blocked except `scene play` of a scene with errors. Pure.

A **pack scene** is a group a pack added (its id is not the game's). Groups with a `Languages` member are pack lines: `PackLineScreen` screens them, so only the script-command rules (S20-S24) run on them here. Rows a pack adds to or overrides in the game's own groups get the script-command rules too.

- **S01 error**: No rows: `ScenarioReader.StartReady` reads row 0 unconditionally.
- **S02 error**: Long story without a Text/ChangeMotion/AddTextLoop/DirectionGameStartCamera row: the pre-scan runs off the end.
- **S03 error**: (Scenario, EpisodeNumber) not unique: every trigger looks groups up by that pair (`FacilityStory`).
- **S04 warning**: Episode below 1000: the mod range starts at 1000 so a game update cannot collide.
- **S05 error**: Extra/AprilFool/Birthday scene the game would offer by itself: ContentType must be a blocking name (`ScenarioGroupMasterWrapper`); the save guard keeps pack scenes unseen, so `None` would be offered again and again (`HeroineAI`).
- **S06 warning**: Long pack scene of a type other than ExtraScenario (story progress and collaboration code read those types).
- **S10 error / S11 warning**: WaitInput, Tutorial stall (the reader has no case for them); ReadNextForScript waits for code, tutorial commands drive the tutorial UI.
- **S12 error**: A Selection/Jump/TutorialSelection/IfBetweenDateTime/StartTextLoop target is not a row of the group.
- **S13 error**: A LocalizationID that does not exist, or none on VoiceText/Selection (the reader's lookup is null and throws).
- **S14 error**: An argument the game parses with float/int.Parse, Enum.Parse or ParseExact would throw.
- **S15 warning**: The row before a branch start falls through into the branch (end it with Jump or EndScenario).
- **S16 warning**: A short scene plays story music or ambience and never stops it (the short EndStory path does not).
- **S20 error**: A script-command row while the seam is not installed: the reader would stall.
- **S21 warning**: A script command no one handles (yet): the row is skipped with a warning.
- **S22 error**: A built-in's Arg1 its handler would refuse ([`ScenarioBuiltInArgs`](#scenariobuiltinargs)).
- **S23 warning**: `cwy.do`/`cwy.defer` names an action that is not registered.
- **S24 warning**: In a long story, a script-command row before the first line never runs (the pre-scan skips to it).
- **S25 warning**: A pack row of a group nobody has: it never plays.

<a id="scenariolint--blockingcontenttypes"></a>

### `static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> BlockingContentTypes`

The ContentType names that keep the game from offering an Extra/AprilFool/Birthday scene (any value but None and PurchaseEnvironment).

<a id="scenariosaverule"></a>

## `ScenarioSaveRule`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioSaveRule` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which scene groups the game's save must never record: the groups a pack added (an id the game's own data does not have). It is the pack-lines save rule (`PackLineSaveFilter`: pack-line ids never reach `ScenarioProgressData.PlayedScenarioGroupIDs` in the file), stated for every pack scene, so the two guards agree: every pack line is a group a pack added (`PackLineScreen`), and this rule keeps the story path out of the save the way pack lines keep small talk out.

Where it applies: the prefix on `Bulbul.FacilityStory.SaveScenarioPlayedLog` (game 1.17.3) skips the whole method for a pack scene, so a long pack scene changes neither the main-story progress (`FinishReadEpisode`), nor a collaboration's progress (`OnEndStory`), nor the played list. A vanilla game therefore loads the save unchanged in meaning, and Steam Cloud carries no mod id.

Consequence the lint enforces (rule S05): a pack scene stays "unseen" to the game, so an Extra scene must carry a ContentType that keeps the game from offering it on its own.

<a id="scenariosaverule--ispackscene"></a>

### `static bool IsPackScene(string groupId, MasterDataBaseline baseline)`

True when the save must not record `groupId`: the game's own ids are known and this is not one of them. False when the baseline is empty (not captured yet): then the game's own code runs unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `groupId`: The group the game is about to log.
- `baseline`: The game's own ids (captured at master-data injection).

<a id="scenariowaitbook"></a>

## `ScenarioWaitBook`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioWaitBook` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The rows a scene is holding on ([`IScenarioCommandContext.WaitFor`](#iscenariocommandcontext--waitfor)): each with its check, deadline and the caller's cursor. The game side polls once a frame and continues the scene for each finished entry. Time is passed in (seconds, any monotonic clock), so this is testable. Thread-safe; checks run on the polling thread outside the lock.

<a id="scenariowaitbook--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

How many rows are holding.

<a id="scenariowaitbook--labels"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Labels { get; }`

Labels of the holding rows, oldest first.

<a id="scenariowaitbook--add"></a>

### `long Add(string label, Func<bool> isDone, TimeSpan timeout, double now, object cursor)`

Starts holding a row.

**Parameters**

- `label`: What is waiting (for logs).
- `isDone`: The check; polled once per [`ScenarioWaitBook.Poll`](#scenariowaitbook--poll).
- `timeout`: The longest hold; negative counts as zero.
- `now`: The current time in seconds.
- `cursor`: The caller's marker of where the scene is; handed back on the end.

**Returns:** A ticket.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `isDone` is null.

<a id="scenariowaitbook--clear"></a>

### `int Clear()`

Drops every holding row (the room unloaded). Nothing continues.

**Returns:** How many were dropped.

<a id="scenariowaitbook--poll"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<ScenarioWaitEnd> Poll(double now, Func<object, bool> stillValid = null)`

Checks every holding row once and removes the finished ones. Order per entry: an entry whose cursor `stillValid` rejects is [`ScenarioWaitEndKind.Abandoned`](#scenariowaitendkind--abandoned) (its check is not run); then the check (true = [`ScenarioWaitEndKind.Done`](#scenariowaitendkind--done), a throw = [`ScenarioWaitEndKind.Threw`](#scenariowaitendkind--threw)); then the deadline ([`ScenarioWaitEndKind.TimedOut`](#scenariowaitendkind--timedout)).

**Parameters**

- `now`: The current time in seconds.
- `stillValid`: True while the scene is still at the entry's cursor; null treats every entry as valid.

**Returns:** The finished entries, in the order they were added; empty when none finished.

<a id="scenariowaitendkind"></a>

## `ScenarioWaitEndKind`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenarioWaitEndKind` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How a held row stopped waiting.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="scenariowaitendkind--done"></a>`Done` | 0 | The check passed. |
| <a id="scenariowaitendkind--timedout"></a>`TimedOut` | 1 | The timeout passed first; the scene goes on with a warning. |
| <a id="scenariowaitendkind--threw"></a>`Threw` | 2 | The check threw; counted as done, with a warning. |

## `ScenePlayPath`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScenePlayPath` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How `scene play` starts a scene.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="sceneplaypath--refused"></a>`Refused` | 0 | It does not. |
| <a id="sceneplaypath--longstory"></a>`LongStory` | 1 | Through the game's own long-story pipeline (`IStoryController.StartStory`): fade, music pause, UI, skip, tidy. |
| <a id="sceneplaypath--clicktalk"></a>`ClickTalk` | 2 | As a click-style talk (`StartReady` + `StartClickHeroineReaction`), the way a click on Satone plays one. |
| <a id="sceneplaypath--gamereplay"></a>`GameReplay` | 3 | A story episode the player has already seen, replayed exactly as the game's history screen does (`StorySelectUI` starts it as a talk-log replay). |
| <a id="sceneplaypath--gamepreview"></a>`GamePreview` | 4 | A game story episode the player has not seen, played only while `[Script] AllowUnseenGameStories` is on: the save folder is backed up first, it plays as a rewatch (`isTalkLog: true`), and the played log is skipped so it is not recorded as seen. |

<a id="scriptactionline"></a>

## `ScriptActionLine`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.ScriptActionLine` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

An action call written in a script row (`cwy.do`, `cwy.defer`): the action name, then `name=value` arguments, in `Arg1`: `music.play title="Rainy Desk" volume=0.5`. Every value is text; the action's typed getters parse it in invariant culture ([`ActionArgs`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actionargs)). Immutable.

Syntax: words split on spaces and tabs; a value in double quotes may hold spaces, with `\"` and `\\` as the only escapes. The name is matched lower-case ([`ActionDescriptor.NamePattern`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actiondescriptor--namepattern)); argument names follow [`ActionParameter.NamePattern`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Actions.md#actionparameter--namepattern) and may not repeat.

<a id="scriptactionline--maxlength"></a>

Longest accepted line.

The arguments, all text values, in the order written.

### `string Name { get; }`

The action name, lower-case.
